Legacy of Gods #1

God of Malice

Rina Kent

3.89
339,913 ratings36,856 reviews
Rate this book
Killian Carson is a predator cloaked in charm. His charisma fools everyone—except Glyndon King. She sees the psychopath beneath and knows she should run. But a dark part of her craves the danger, knowing he’ll chase her . . . and she might just want to be caught.

Glyndon has never been anyone’s favorite, always falling short of her family's expectations. But Killian? He doesn’t expect anything except that she’s his now. Their schools are rivals, their families lifelong enemies, but none of that matters to him.

Can two broken souls heal each other, or will their twisted desires tear them apart? As their pasts collide in more disturbing ways than they imagined, it could either strengthen their bond or be their undoing.

This book is a dark unconventional romance and contains themes that aren't to everyone's liking. Please check the author's note for content warnings before reading.

About the author

Rina Kent

65 books75.5k followers
Rina Kent is a New York Times, USA Today, and #1 bestselling author of all things dark romance.
Better known for writing unapologetic anti-heroes and villains, Rina weaves tales of characters you shouldn’t fall for but inevitably do. Her stories are laced with a touch of darkness, a splash of angst, and just the right amount of unhealthy intensity.
When she’s not busy plotting mayhem for her ever-expanding Rinaverse, she leads a private life in London, travels, and pampers her cats in true Cat Lady fashion.

God of Malice by Rina Kent 🖤🔪

I have questions… HOW is this considered romance?! 🫣 I’m sorry, but I’m not romanticizing a rapist psycho just because he occasionally says something sweet or claims he wants to protect her. Yes, Killian is protective of Glyndon, but he’s also possessive to an extreme and treats her more like an object he owns than a person with actual feelings.

~I have not a shadow of a doubt that the little rabbit is flipping my world upside down. And I’ll let her. Because she’s mine. And I’ll set the whole fucking world on fire to make sure she remains safe.~

Sir, you can say all the sweet things you want, but this man isn’t just dark… he’s the PITCHIEST OF BLACK. 🥴🖤

For anyone unfamiliar, God of Malice follows Glyndon, an art student who catches the attention of Killian Carson, a dangerously manipulative man who becomes obsessed with her. Their relationship spirals into a twisted dynamic of power, control, and obsession that pushes boundaries in some seriously disturbing ways.

And Glyndon? Girl, WHERE IS YOUR BACKBONE?! 😭 She often felt like a doormat, letting Killian control her and push her around. Not that he exactly respects the word no anyway. In fact, he seems to enjoy it when she defies him, which makes their dynamic even more disturbing.

I can appreciate that the plot was decent, and I’m not going to let one book determine how I feel about the entire series. But there were SO many things about this one that just gave me the ick. 🫣

God of Malice was disturbing, uncomfortable, and, somehow, still an interesting read. I had my complaints, but there were aspects I enjoyed, even if I couldn’t fully get on board with the romance.

And honestly? I already love several of the side characters and cannot WAIT for their stories! 👀🖤 I’m excited to see what the rest of the series has in store for me.

I keep saying Rina Kent’s books are trash, but then I also keep reading them. What does that make me? Her trash can?

“I have not a shadow of a doubt that the little rabbit is flipping my world upside down. And I’ll let her. Because she’s mine. And I’ll set the whole fucking world on fire to make sure she remains safe.”


I was never expecting to like this book, that’s why I went in with no expectations. I just knew I would hate it, but the joke’s on me because I ended up enjoying it more than I thought I would. This book had me questioning my taste in books and fictional men, and I tried hating it, but it was just so addictive and toxic. I was eating up every damn chapter. God of Malice gave me some serious war flashbacks from Haunting Adeline with the cliff scene. I was so ready to hate it after that, but then it got better, I guess, in terms of plot and romance. I really liked the new setup for the second generation, it’s giving Royal Elite x Elite vibes but on steroids.

“Whatever you’re willing to do in exchange for my chivalrous act of saving a damsel in distress.”


Killian is a true feminist. He believes in the “it’s her choice” principle because he gave her a choice to decide what she wants him to do with her body, but he’s also a very sweet person, so he narrowed it down to three options so his girl wouldn’t stress herself out by making such hard decisions in an already stressful situation. He’s truly a gentleman, one who may not know the meaning of consent but would make a masterpiece out of the girl he’s obsessed with by throwing her off a cliff. And he’s not bad; he’s just a misunderstood villain with a psychotic diagnosis that makes him a flawed person, not a bad one. Potato, potahto.

“Listen to me and listen to me well, Glyndon. I spent my whole life repressing my true nature, but I’d willingly embrace my demons for you. I’d turn into the devil, a monster, and whatever weapon I have to be if it means I can protect you.”


Killian is also hilarious because how many times do you find a character who’s studying to become a doctor just because he has urges to cut open living things to see inside their bodies, and it’s illegal and criminal in reality, so he took a more reasonable approach to fulfil his desires? Killian is nice because he always listens to Glyn, always knows what she wants because he understands her desires more than she does, even when she doesn’t tell him about them. He listens to her—just not when she tells him “No”. But semantics. He’s unhinged and dangerous and brooding, but you can never go wrong with this man. He’s one in a million.

“You’d allow yourself to be used?”
“By you? Absolutely.” And I mean that shit. If this woman asks me to cut my chest open and show her the organ she’s asked for, I’d rip it from its tendons and lay it at her feet.


Glyndon was nice but also boring. She had her moments, and she’s much better than Astrid and Elsa, and that says something. She’s an artist dealing with depression, inferiority complex, and an existential crisis, but it’s sad how that wasn’t discussed in detail. It was just magically healed by Killian because he made her courageous and confident about herself. I didn’t know men had magical healing abilities or is Killian just special? I didn’t like how the cliff scene was overlooked by the fact that Glyn likes being forced, even when she said no. It was sexual assault and rape, and she had just met Killian for the first time so how can she feel that way about him and Rina tried to justify it by giving an explanation about how she always has a Non-Con kink? And don’t get me started on the virginity kink because it’s not a Rina Kent book if the MMC isn’t obsessed with the FMC’s virgin blood.

“For a moment, you want to stop being a good girl and just let whatever lurks inside you loose, isn’t that right?”


Killian and Glyndon have chemistry! Shocker, but they actually made sense together as a couple. I liked them together, and they even had some decent emotional moments that made me root for them. Killian became soft and caring towards Glyn in the second half, and I liked how they understood each other so well. There’s definitely something wrong with both of them, but they chose to ignore it and instead fell in love. So who am I to judge them when I liked this book?

“Understand this, Glyndon, there’s nothing noble or tender about what I feel for you. It’s a violent volcano of obsession, possession, and deranged lust. If you want love, then I do love you, but it’s the unorthodox version of love. I love you enough to let you within my walls. I love you enough to let you talk to my demons. I love you enough to allow you to have a hold over me when I’ve never allowed anyone to have the power to destroy me from the inside out.”


I liked the side characters, and they all seemed better than Kill and Glyn. I liked Jeremy and his overprotective personality. Cecily was a cute nerd. Cray Cray is the cutest grump. Annika is also cute, but she talks too much. Landon and his overprotectiveness over Glyn is NOT hot. Brandon is so precious and nice. Nikolai is unhinged, but in an adorable way. Ava and her Barbie personality annoyed me. Eli was non-existent. Remi was so unintentionally hilarious. Gareth was also nice, I guess. The parents’ POV was such a jumpscare, especially Reina and Asher’s. This was a good start to the series. Hope it stays that way.

He’s never cared for girls, never had girlfriends, never wanted to be in a relationship, and, well, now he does 💁🏻‍♀️. She might say no, but he doesn’t care 😂. They’re together whether she likes it or not 🙃

—how duuuurty his mouth is 🥵. Are you kidding me Killian? How dare you be this good? You have no business being such a f!lthy speaking 19 year-old 💦. Good LAWD. Save my kindle. Killian has spoken and it’s gonna melt 🔥

—how OTT and JP Killian is. I mean. This man sees his woman getting near OM and he goes ape ish. I love me some jealous OM scenes, and this one is GOOD 😈💅
”Looks like I created a monster. Maybe we should explore your sexuality, after all.” “Exploring my sexuality means sleeping around, hooking up. You know, the casual kinky sex you had but I didn’t get the chance to try.” My smirk disappears. “If you’re up for fucking in their blood, then sure thing. You have the green light to pick some poor souls.”


—the soft side of Killian. Yeah, I know. Seems weird, but he has some swoony moments. Not too many lol but considering he’s not well versed in sweet or nice, I was pleasantly surprised

—the side characters. I found myself taking notes as to who was doing what and who’s kid was whose and what family did what 🤣. I have to say, having read many of the books from the parents of the kids, I appreciated seeing their offsprings lol. I even noticed how similar certain kids were to their parents. I mean. The apple doesn’t fall far from the tree 💅

—Remi and his lordship was annoying, yet also hilarious omg. Reminds me of his dad 😂. He gets his own bullet (since he won’t be getting a book 😩 neither is Gareth 🥺 and a few other characters)

—the text messages!!! Not only between the kids, but THE LAST TEXTING THREAD WAS SOOO SOOO GOOD! Sigh. Man. I’m feeling like I need to revisit RES. I was legit GIDDY and smiling !!!

—the parents’ POV chapters. I need to read Killian’s parents’ duet, but I still got the gist

—the rivalry stuff that’s happening. Obviously, there’s going to be an overarching storyline as the series progresses. I’m excited 🥰

—potential couples 👀. I found myself analyzing all the interactions between characters as they were meeting. I’m soo excited for book 2 👏🏻

—the ow stuff 😑. Now. If you’ve read my reviews, you know how much I hate it in my books, but in this one, I like how Killian puts the ow in her place. He stops her kisses and talks shit to her 💁🏻‍♀️. Sounds good to me 💅

What I didn’t like/wanted more of:
—when the tension between Killian and his family happens, I wanted it to be drawn out more. I got emotional, regardless, but I still wanted more

—more sweet Killian. He actually makes an effort, but I would’ve liked to see them as a nice couple a little bit longer (like in an extended epilogue lol). I get it. We’ll get their HEA as the series continues, but I wanted more

—there were some grammar/spelling mistakes. If the mistakes are minor, I tend to overlook them, but there were a couple that had me rereading lines to figure out what was supposed to be there 😬

Overall, I pretty much loved it lol. It’s been a while since I read a good Rina Kent book, and this one hit all my spots 😉
